data: China's first large hydrogen engine — the Long March 5 core
China's first large hydrogen engine — Long March 5's foundation

The YF-77 is China's first large-scale cryogenic engine burning LOX and LH2, ending a multi-decade dependence on storable hypergolic propellants for core stages. Developed by AALPT and running a gas-generator cycle, two YF-77s power Long March 5's central core, providing the efficiency boost that made lunar-return and space-station-module missions achievable without a prohibitively large rocket. It first flew on 3 November 2016, and the early flights were not without difficulty — a YF-77 anomaly grounded Long March 5 for nearly three years before engineers identified and resolved the failure mode.
